hints.title: Same-Employee Shift Pairing
hints.text: Two shifts belong to the same employee and overlap if the second starts after the first starts but before the first ends.

hints.title: Strict Inequality for Deduplication
hints.text: Imposing Shift1.start_time < Shift2.start_time ensures each pair of overlapping shifts is counted exactly once and self-matches are excluded.

hints.title: Count Aggregation
hints.text: Group by employee id and count the number of matching join records, ordering output by employee id ascending.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT 
    Shift1.employee_id, 
    COUNT(*) AS overlapping_shifts 
FROM EmployeeShifts AS Shift1
INNER JOIN EmployeeShifts AS Shift2 
    ON Shift1.employee_id = Shift2.employee_id
    AND Shift1.start_time < Shift2.start_time 
    AND Shift2.start_time < Shift1.end_time
GROUP BY Shift1.employee_id
ORDER BY Shift1.employee_id ASC;
```

variables: s: total number of shift records
complexity.notes: Self-join on indexed employee id with range filter.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Cartesian cross joins across distinct employees degrade performance.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Uses self-join with strict inequality to avoid double counting overlapping intervals.
